title: The embed stage dominates segment-mode refreshes under CPU contention
notes: Mini refresh 14:29-15:24: embed 14:45:28-15:18:23 for 394 records (256 in 427.8 s, then 138 in 1509.7 s, 11 s/record), against 1.3 s/record on 2026-11-05. CPU samples 14:10-14:55: mini total 466 % of 800 % on average, mostly `node` from other sessions; atrium 49 % average, 373 % peak. Next: measure the ONNX embedder's threads against the free cores. Correction 2026-11-09: the priority half is already in place, `atrium-refresh` renices the whole pipeline to 10 since 2026-10-19, so the 11 s/record above was measured at nice 10; `cpu_session_options` sets no `intra_op_num_threads`, so ONNX starts one thread per core whatever is free. The new per-stage CPU lines (dotfiles `9e0bbe1`) give the embed stage's CPU beside its wall time. First reading, MacBook 2026-11-09 01:56-01:59: embed used 12 min 17 s of CPU in 2 min 32 s (about 4.8 cores at nice 10), 79% of the whole refresh's CPU. Measured threads the same night (64 texts, load 14-16, `nice 10`): every core and spinning 3.3-3.5 s / 25-26 CPU-s; every core, spinning off 2.9 s / 16.5 CPU-s; 4 threads, spinning off 3.2 s / 10.5; 2 threads 3.8 s / 7.4. Spinning off is better on both axes, so `atrium embed` now opts in (`batch_session_options`, atrium `dae25c3`); the reranker lost 10-15% latency without spinning and races its 3 s budget, so query paths keep the default. Left: the embed stage's CPU on the next refresh with embeds to do, against the 12 min 17 s above, and whether a thread cap (2-4) is worth its 10-30% wall time.
